All benchmarks are English logical reasoning; FOLIO and ProofWriter represent a best-case for symbolic verification, and the observed bias ratios ($1.66$--$4.97\times$) likely represent a \emph{lower bound} on SCB in less structured domains. Statistical power is limited for effects below ${\sim}2$\,pp (MDE $1.86$--$4.84$\,pp across conditions); small positive effects cannot be ruled out. We do not evaluate trained extractors, which could potentially break the self-extraction bound by introducing external signal. The cross-architecture escape (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) is validated with a single NLI architecture (DeBERTa); whether the capability-gap pattern generalizes to other verifier types (e.g., code executors, proof assistants) remains open. Our formal analysis assumes source-attribution scoring; alternative attribution schemes that decouple constraints from their originating traces could alter the degeneration condition, though no such scheme has been proposed.
